overview: The Dunmore Mine developed a complex polymetallic lode in the Ouray–Uncompahgre mining district.
moreHistory: Kelley and Caswell Silver describes a persistent fissure zone more than two miles long, averaging nearly 100 feet wide along the Dunmore claim.

Its productive mineralization included a hematite chimney enclosing a copper shoot, a tungsten chimney, and compound base-metal fissure veins—an unusual combination that helped geologists connect the chimney-style and vein-style deposits of the San Juan Mountains.
Federal exploration records document renewed interest in the Dunmore and related Yankee Lad claims during the 1950s, including tungsten investigation.
Modern locality records document aerial-tram-station and cable remnants below the mine, but the exact present condition of every structure has not been independently field-verified.

Component safeguard: keep the Dunmore workings, the Yankee Lad claim, tramway and terminal remnants, and nearby Red Mountain or Idarado properties as separate linked elements unless claim mapping proves a tighter identity.
